name: pivot
domain: A Next.js 14 recipe-sharing site (app router, TypeScript, Tailwind) is adding realtime collaborative shopping lists: every recipe page gets a shared shopping list that several visitors can edit together and see each other on. The session first builds a hand-rolled WebSocket server with custom presence, then pivots mid-way to Supabase Realtime channels after hitting serverless deploy constraints.

phases.goal: Kickoff. The user asks for realtime collaborative shopping lists on recipe pages. Assistant and user agree the scope: each recipe page owns exactly one shared shopping list keyed by its slug (plant F1). They choose approach A: a dedicated hand-rolled WebSocket server using the ws package, run as a separate Node process on port 3001 next to Next.js (plant the T1 supersededEvidence in assistant prose recommending this). They also agree item toggles are optimistic with server echo reconciliation (plant F2). Assistant writes server/realtime-server.js (ws server with a room per list slug) and src/lib/listProtocol.ts (message types). The user also asks to scaffold a big seed catalog of recipes for testing, which lands as the bulk asset src/data/recipes.ts.

Build out approach A. Assistant writes the client hook src/hooks/useListSocket.ts that connects to ws://localhost:3001 (plant the T3 supersededEvidence when describing how components consume it), and adds custom presence to the server: track peers ourselves with an in memory Map of socket ids (plant the T2 supersededEvidence in assistant prose), with a heartbeat that pings every 15 seconds and evicts peers after two missed beats (plant F3). A bug appears while testing: React strict mode double mounts the effect and duplicates every socket subscription (plant F13); assistant fixes it with a cleanup + ref guard in useListSocket. The user also asks for sample collaborator accounts for local testing, landing as the bulk asset src/data/sampleUsers.ts.

The pivot. The user tries to plan deployment and reports the blocker: the site deploys to Vercel serverless, and Vercel serverless gives us no sticky sessions and kills long lived sockets (plant F4 in the user or assistant turn discussing the blocker). After weighing options (separate Fly.io box rejected as extra ops burden), the user decides: we will move the whole realtime layer onto Supabase Realtime channels (plant F5). Assistant confirms the consequence explicitly: the hand rolled socket server is dead, Supabase Realtime replaces it entirely (plant T1 currentEvidence). They sketch the migration plan: create a shopping_items table, swap the hook, port presence to channel presence.

Rip out A, build B. Assistant deletes the approach A files and says plainly that it deleted server/realtime-server.js and src/hooks/useListSocket.ts in the cleanup (plant F6), and notes useListSocket is deleted; components import useShoppingList instead (plant T3 currentEvidence). New code: src/lib/supabaseClient.ts and src/hooks/useShoppingList.ts, where useShoppingList subscribes to postgres_changes on the shopping_items table (plant F7). SQL migration discussed in chat: enable row level security on shopping_items with an anon read policy (plant F8). Presence is ported too: Supabase channel presence now tracks peers so the heartbeat Map is gone (plant T2 currentEvidence). The user also asks for a polish pass of shared utility styles for the list UI, landing as the bulk asset src/styles/list-utilities.css.

Mid-task wiring of B's presence indicator. Assistant creates src/components/PresenceAvatars.tsx where PresenceAvatars renders one colored dot per peer from presenceState (plant F9), and wires it into ShoppingList. They decide the presence key is the anon session id we stash in localStorage (plant F12). Testing in two browser tabs shows the bug the session ends on: join events render fine but leave events still never remove the avatar (plant F10) - the assistant is mid-investigation, suspecting the presence leave callback is not re-rendering because the handler mutates state in place; a fix is proposed but NOT yet applied. The user restates the remaining roadmap: after presence lands we still owe the typing broadcast and a deploy preview (plant F11). The phase ends with the fix still pending.
